layer_vocabulary.notes: rules (the Decision layer): staged pipeline in tools/approval.py — parse floor (malformed quoting fails closed) -> hardline blocklist (UNRECOVERABLE_BLOCKLIST, forbidden, no override) -> approvals.deny fnmatch globs (forbidden, unconditional, all backends) -> command_allowlist/session approvals (silent allow) -> DANGEROUS_PATTERNS trigger table (~40 documented rows) routed by approvals.mode; plus a separate write_file/patch protected-path denylist (forbidden, no prompt) and a website blocklist for web/browser tools. approval (the Approval layer): CLI once/session/always/deny dialog; gateway reply/button asks; smart-mode guardian LLM (STOCHASTIC, default mode — an Approval-layer mechanism, never a decision oracle); timeout 300s fail-closed deny; cron/single_query/unattended context modes default deny; DM pairing + allowlists gate who may be asked. sandbox (part of the Effect layer — OS-level confinement): terminal backends local/ssh (no isolation, checks ON) vs docker/modal/daytona/vercel_sandbox/singularity (isolated, dangerous-command checks SKIPPED — container is the boundary; approvals.deny still applies); Docker hardening flags documented; HERMES_WRITE_SAFE_ROOT confines write_file/patch only (vendor: defense-in-depth, terminal bypasses it). effect (the Effect layer — observed outcome): env-var stripping for terminal/execute_code children, MCP safe-vars-only environment, optional checkpoints; agent self-report explicitly distrusted by the vendor (file-mutation verifier).

spike_answers.a_native_oracle: NO. The documented top-level CLI surface (chat, model, gateway, auth, config, doctor, security audit, approvals, prompt-size, sessions, cron, hooks, mcp, acp, serve, etc.) contains no check/evaluate/dry-run/policy-test entrypoint. Near-misses are not oracles: 'hermes approvals suggest' mines past approval history from the session DB into allowlist proposals; 'hermes config check' checks config completeness; 'hermes security audit' is a supply-chain (OSV.dev) audit; 'hermes prompt-size' runs offline but reports prompt bytes. The decision function (tools/approval.py detect_dangerous_command) is an internal function covering only the detection stage, and in the default smart mode the flagged-command outcome is decided by an auxiliary LLM — the harness's own full decision is stochastic by design in its default configuration, so there is no deterministic decision function to replay.
spike_answers.b_documented_semantics: YES, for a bounded deterministic subset. Documented precisely across three agreeing vendor surfaces: (1) hardline blocklist (code-shipped UNRECOVERABLE_BLOCKLIST; forbidden regardless of yolo/mode off/'allow always'; trips before the approval layer; pattern table vendor-marked 'not exhaustive'; unparseable quoting fails closed); (2) approvals.deny — case-insensitive fnmatch globs over the whole command text and extracted executable candidates, with documented normalization/deobfuscation, quote-aware compound splitting (; && || pipelines groups substitutions), a named launcher-unwrapping list (sudo/env/command/timeout/...), recursive shell -c inspection, and basename-vs-literal-path candidate rules; blocks unconditionally before yolo/off, on all backends; (3) a ~40-row dangerous-pattern trigger table (rm -r, mkfs, dd if=, DROP TABLE, DELETE FROM without WHERE, curl|sh, bash -c, find -delete, ...) routed by mode — manual -> prompt, smart (default) -> guardian LLM (STOCHASTIC, excluded from evaluation), off/yolo -> execute; timeout 300s default -> deny; cron/single-query/unattended modes default deny; (4) command_allowlist (exact/glob/rule-key) silently approves, incl. on unattended surfaces; (5) write_file/patch protected-path denylist (forbidden, no prompt; ~/.ssh/config approval-gated exception) + optional HERMES_WRITE_SAFE_ROOT. No-match on local/ssh backends executes unflagged (execution default -> framework unknown, never allow). Ceilings: full regex lists unpublished; vendor-documented normalization limits (variables/aliases/functions/renamed binaries/scripts/case-patterns unresolved); container backends skip dangerous-command checks (approvals.deny excepted); execute_code payloads escape the pattern layer; plugin/shell hooks are arbitrary code; deny-vs-allowlist precedence not explicitly documented; session/always approval state is part of the decision function.
